title: Mindfulness of the body
hook: a bad mirror morning, and an old picture: the body as a sack of grains, sorted by someone with good eyes
tomorrow: of all the things to watch, why the breath?

segments.voice: Yesterday, maranasati: death is certain, its hour isn't, and the quarrels get smaller. From the end of the body, to the body itself.

The front camera opens by accident, and there's your face from below, in bad light, before coffee. A whole verdict arrives in half a second. The Buddha offers a very different way of looking, and it comes with a strange picture. A bag, open at both ends, full of mixed grains: hill rice, paddy, green gram, kidney beans, sesame. Someone with good eyes unties it and sorts. That's rice. Those are beans. That's sesame. No verdict at all.
screen: `THE FRONT CAMERA, BY ACCIDENT.` → `A VERDICT IN HALF A SECOND.` → `A SACK OF MIXED GRAINS.`

segments.voice: The picture comes from the Satipatthana Sutta. Review this body, the Buddha says, from the soles of the feet up and from the hair down, as full of many kinds of things: head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, and on through what's inside. Then the bag of grains, and the one who names each kind. The Visuddhimagga calls this kayagatasati, mindfulness of the body, and teaches learning the list by heart, aloud first, then silently, forward and back. Tradition says the first five, head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, are given to a new monk at ordination. The earlier days on the body's changes were about cooling desire. This one is quieter. It's about seeing. A lot of what hurts in front of a mirror is the story on top: too much, not enough, not like that photo. The sack doesn't argue back. It's just known.
screen: `FROM THE FEET UP, THE HAIR DOWN.` · `NAME EACH GRAIN.` · `ALOUD, THEN SILENTLY.` · `SEEING, NOT JUDGING.` · then, large: `THE BODY KNOWN.`

segments.voice: Look at one hand, palm up, and name what's there the way the sutta does: skin, nails, the lines, the bones under it, the veins at the wrist. No verdict and no comparing, just the list; whenever a story starts, go back to naming.
Mindfulness of the body: reviewing the body part by part, plainly, like grains in a sack. Neither admired nor despised. Known.
The line to keep: the body known, not judged, from the hair down to the soles. Twenty-six days into the forty.

screen: `DAY 1531 COUNTS.` → `FORTY SUBJECTS · 26 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: OF ALL THINGS, WHY THE BREATH?`

howItsDone: Theravada meditators learn the parts of the body as a recited list, first aloud and then silently; the first five parts are traditionally taught to new monks at ordination.

fork.setup: your little sister comes home upset: kids said her arms are hairy. she asks what's wrong with her. what fits the grain-sack way of seeing?

fork.reveal: the sutta names what's there and stops. the verdict, ugly or perfect, is the story on top, and the practice sets it down.
